text:
matt: Heads up — hitting bizarre generation diffs after converting a HF jinja chat_template to Redwood prompt format. Minimal repro below, curious if anyone else has seen empty assistant blocks survive conversion and break the tokenizer -> model input alignment.

matt: HF jinja template (trimmed):
```jinja
{% for msg in conversation %}
{{ msg.role }}: {{ msg.content | default("") }}
{% endfor %}
```

matt: In a few cases `msg.content` is an empty string for assistant placeholders (used by the HF conversation builder). HF ends up emitting a blank assistant turn, e.g. `assistant: ` (no content). Redwood conversion produced role markers and a stray ` ` token sequence that shifted tokenization for the following user prompt.

anya: Interesting — do you have the converted Redwood prompt (what our converter outputs)?

matt: Converter output (simplified):
```text
<|system|>You are helpful.
<|assistant|>
<|user|>Please summarize the following...
```

anya: Ah — that empty `<|assistant|>` token is the problem. Tokenizers treat that delimiter differently depending on model vs tokenizer config, and with quantized kernels small shifts produce different next-token probs.

lee: Two angles: 1) HF chat templates sometimes use empty assistant messages as placeholders for streaming/response assembly; 2) our HF->Redwood conversion should drop assistant turns where content is empty or only default whitespace. We need to be careful with explicit special tokens though (models that rely on sentinel tokens).

nate: Also watch config.json `add_bos` / `sep_token` behavior. Some HF model configs set `pad_token = ""` or rely on `bos_token` implicitness; when converter maps those tokens into our prompt wrapper it can duplicate tokens. That duplication looks like an empty role marker but is actually a token sequence.

sam: Repro note: this was most visible after quantizing to int8 - small token shifts amplified by quantization noise produced coherent but wrong continuations. If you can reproduce, please attach the tokenized ids before and after conversion.

matt: Attached token diffs (excerpt):
```
# before conversion (HF template collapsed): [101, 102, 200, 345]
# after conversion (empty assistant preserved): [101, 50256, 200, 345]
# 50256 = <|assistant|> token id on this tokenizer
```

lee: Solution proposal: converter step should: 1) detect assistant/user/system roles with empty content; 2) if empty and not explicitly required by model (check list of models with sentinel semantics), drop the role marker entirely; 3) if model requires sentinel, replace with a single canonical placeholder token we control (e.g. `[ASSISTANT_PLACEHOLDER]`) and map that in config.json so tokenizers stay consistent.

anya: +1. Add a unit test that loads a few HF chat_template variants (empty assistant, default filter, jinja if/else branch that yields nothing) and asserts the serialized prompt tokens are identical to our expected gold.

nate: Also add a transformer in the onboarding pipeline to normalize `config.json` fields: explicitly set `eos_token`, `bos_token`, `pad_token` if missing and record any original values in metadata. That will help avoid silent differences across tokenizers when converting.

infra-bot: model-onboard-job #482 failed: converter returned non-deterministic prompt for model redwood-test-quant-1 — logs attached.

sam: I'll pick up the converter patch. Plan: filter empty assistant/user/system turns unless the model is in the sentinel-exception list; add tests; add a small migration that maps old onboarding configs to normalized tokenizer tokens.

matt: Thanks — if you can land a hotfix we can re-run the quantization eval and check for the regression. For the record, we should also add a small eval case in Optimize that detects any token-offset behavior pre/post-conversion (simple perplexity diff on a held prompt set).

lee: Agreed. I'll add to the onboarding checklist: "verify no empty role markers survive HF->RW conversion" and a note about sentinel-token models.

matt: Cool — tagging @sam to track. :thumbsup:
